justification.text: `1 / (↑n - ↑a)` is the problem's summand 1/(n - a) with the subtraction in ℝ (no truncation), and its denominator is positive because the hypothesis `a < n` on every a ∈ A gives n - a ≥ 1, matching A ⊆ [1, n).
p ranges over the primes below n (`(range n).filter Prime`), so p ≥ 2 and 1/p is never a division by zero; this is the docstring's Σ_{p<n} 1/p.
`1 ≤ a ∧ a < n` is the docstring's 'A ⊆ [1, n)': integers from 1 inclusive to n exclusive.

open Finset

theorem Opn.erdos_1210 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℕ,
      (∀ a ∈ A, 1 ≤ a ∧ a < n) →
      (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, a ≠ b → a.Coprime b) →
      ∑ a ∈ A, (1 / ((n : ℝ) - a)) ≤ (∑ p ∈ (range n).filter Prime, (1 / (p : ℝ))) + C := by
  sorry
